legend: This gross pathology picture of a bone surface tumour demonstrates a well-delineated and circumscribed tumour with zonal white cartilaginous (closer to bone surface) and tan-pink solid components.
Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma may uncommonly show spindle cell morphology and eosinophilic matrix resembling osteoid.
Staghorn or pericytoid vascular pattern present in the undifferentiated area.
A round cell tumour of undifferentiated tumour cells, which may be seen in small biopsies.
Round cells with central zonal cartilage and bone.
Linear progression from resting chondrocytes to proliferating to hypertrophic to endochondral ossification to bone.

diagnosis: Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma involving the left pedicle of the eighth thoracic vertebra
legend: CT showing an osteolytic and destructive lesion with irregular calcification accompanied by extraosseous extension into the soft tissue in the vertebral foramen and spinal canal.
